prompts.task: Audit the AO resource/environment configuration plan for the live FastAPI app and independent eval_runner.py in ./service. No new live Project or Agent Stream names have been accepted. Inventory actual startup/profile loading, evaluation selectors and live SDK selectors with their source-backed precedence. Assess missing live bindings, required user inputs, resource lookup/reuse/create and failure behavior, and the actual profile and launcher changes a later selected implementation would need. Preserve effective operator configuration and distinguish proposed live defaults from accepted inputs and independent evaluation settings. Write and validate canonical .observe audit JSON and its reader output. Do not modify application code, dependencies, env/config profiles or tests, install an SDK, start services, provision resources, make cloud calls or broaden into GenAI instrumentation.

judge_inputs: Inspect Makefile, app.py, eval_runner.py, README.md, pyproject.toml, actual configuration sources, and canonical audit plus reader output.
rubric: Inventories actual launch/profile loading and source-native SPLUNK_AO_EVAL_PROJECT/SPLUNK_AO_EVAL_STREAM selectors, including their explicit defaults and precedence. Separately inventories supported standard SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT(_ID)/SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM(_ID) live SDK selectors and identifies the live app's absent binding. Does not assume standard vars override evaluation source arguments, reuse evaluation names as live configuration, or treat missing application binding as proof that cloud resources are absent.

Rule: Plans the required Project and Agent Stream inputs for new AO work without auto-accepting blank fields, configured values or suggested names. Preserves effective application selectors and discloses stable source-derived live Project and <service-name>-live stream proposals only for missing values. Assigns later selected work a concrete actual profile update and supported runner loading step; the audit changes no profile, provisions nothing and exposes no credentials.
Example: A proposed live name remains a suggestion while the finding identifies which real application profile and launcher must consume accepted inputs.
Evidence: Reconcile the canonical resource findings with Makefile/process loading, existing configuration and the source-supported service identity. Assess the plan and input provenance, not rendered field or command behavior.
Insufficient evidence: An unused example profile, silently accepting a default or evaluation name as the live target, erasing an effective selector, provisioning during audit, or exposing credentials.

Uses distinct selectable Project, Agent Stream, and routing findings where each live gap exists, preserving stream/project dependency and ordinary telemetry scope. Required fixes/acceptance include exact reuse for both-existing, creation of selected definitively missing named resources, mixed-state minimal creation, project ownership validation, bounded exact duplicate-conflict relookup, and no speculative creation after auth/outage lookup failure. No selected AO work means no creation; gateway absence blocks only gateway-specific live proof and never the implementation or local fake-test plan.

Rule: Preserves legacy target compatibility and creation restrictions in the plan without treating a valid incomplete packet as ready for new instrumentation. A saved creation prohibition remains effective; IDs remain lookup-only and are not reinterpreted as names. Policy-only or partial targets still need the complete required destination inputs, and accepting those inputs does not authorize unselected resource work.
Example: A saved create_if_missing=false policy is retained while missing destination inputs are requested before new work; an unresolved legacy ID does not trigger replacement creation.
Evidence: Check the canonical plan against the current AO contract and the service’s actual targets and restrictions. Require saved-ID or policy-only compatibility checks when those inputs exist; missing discussion of absent hypothetical packets is not a failure. In every plan, allow creation only when the selection permits it, and keep reuse-only effective. Reject any plan that overrides a creation restriction, accepts an incomplete destination, replaces an unresolved supplied ID, or adds unselected resource work. Grade the plan and its scope, rather than whether a generated command succeeds.
Insufficient evidence: Silently reenabling creation, treating blank or partial values as an accepted destination, replacing an unresolved ID, or expanding selected work merely because a destination was supplied.
